headline: Builder Clayco says the main structure of the first part of the Project Jupiter data center campus in New Mexico is finished and the project is more than 25% complete.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: an opinion column by the builder, whose progress and job figures are unverified company claims.
importance_line: People in Doña Ana County are told of jobs and low water use, but the figures are the builder's own and the column does not mention the power delays reported in September, when Oracle sent a legal notice over delayed power supply.
summary: In an opinion column in the Albuquerque Journal, Bob Clark, an executive at the construction firm Clayco, says Clayco and fellow builder Kiewit have placed the final structural beam on the 855,000-square-foot first part of Project Jupiter, a data center campus being built with Oracle in Doña Ana County, New Mexico, and that the project is now more than 25% complete. The column also promises closed-loop cooling that will not use community drinking water and projects more than 7,000 construction jobs, claims that are the company's own.
notes: Opinion column by Bob Clark of Clayco (author from the page's structured data), so the figures are company claims. A column titled 'Building Project Jupiter for southern New Mexico' ran in the Las Cruces Sun-News on 3 Oct 2026 (page not readable here, so not confirmed as the same text); the milestone itself is undated. Earlier Project Jupiter items: our 25 Sep and 27 Sep 2026 editions (Oracle force majeure notice over delayed power).
